text:
isabel: FYI I ran a quick bring-up test on the new quant4 build and hit a consistent divergence when prefill introduces sparse ANCHOR tokens that sit just inside the context window edge (around 64k tokens).
cheng: ugh, interesting. divergence between cached vs cold-run?
isabel: yes — cold-run (no KV) and hot-run (with KV reuse) agree until ~+2048 tokens after anchor, then logits drift.
noah: can you paste the minimal repro command?
isabel: sure: 

```
# local repro harness
python tests/longctx_repro.py --model magnet-65k-q4 --input tests/fixtures/anchor_spike_64k.txt --use-kv-cache true --seed 42
```

metrics: KL between hot/cold grows to 0.15 by token+4096, wp diff visible in top-5.
sam: does it happen on float32 too or only quantized?
isabel: float32 also shows tiny drift but magnitude << quant4. quantized int4/quant4 amplifies it.
lucy-ml: could be RoPE phase wrap/aliasing near window boundary + quant rounding. did you test with scaled rotary (pos_scale) off vs on?
isabel: tested pos_scale=1.0 vs 0.999, small change but still drift.
cheng: isolate whether it's prefill alignment vs cache indexing: try filling with neutral tokens (spaces) vs complex tokens. if neutral tokens don't reproduce, it's a priming interaction.
isabel: good call. did that: neutral filler reduces but doesn't eliminate. pattern: anchors that have high-frequency token IDs cause stronger drift.
noah: ops ask: which commit/sha? we need to bisect kernel changes if it's runtime.
isabel: run on: rwd/serving@e3f9d7c, model artifact v2.1-q4.
ci-bot: canary test run queued: test-run/1777771234-1 started on qtest-ml-12
ops-bot: note, this host has prefetch enabled by default, suggest toggling --disable-prefetch for comparison.
sam: also try disabling KV prefetch and set kv-stride to 1 (no prefetch)
isabel: did that: --disable-prefetch removed early divergence for ~60% of samples, but some still diverged later.
cheng: hypothesis: fractional index mapping when slicing RoPE embeddings into quantized tiles. Could be an off-by-one when cached indices cross tile boundary.
lucy-ml: can you dump KV index stamps for the run? a tiny script to print the last 16 indices + their token ids should show wrap.
isabel: added this quick dump to the repro harness: 
```
# kv dump snippet
for i in range(kv.len-16, kv.len):
    print(i, kv.index[i], kv.token_id[i])
```

attached logs: shows index jump from 65534 -> 2 in one case (wrap), even though expected wrap at 65536.
noah: that smells like modulo mismatch, maybe using 16-bit vs 32-bit counters somewhere. runtime uses uint16 for kv offset in the quant path?
cheng: on quant flow we did pack offsets into uint16 in a perf patch. if buffer length > 65535 that will wrap. but our contexts are 65536 tokens so corner case.
sam: edge case indeed. what about long window modes where we shard kv across pages? does shard join handle carry?
isabel: joining code shows `offset = (offset + stride) & 0xFFFF` in a couple places. should be 0xFFFFFFFF for 32-bit.
lucy-ml: ok that's actionable. can we hotfix to use 32-bit counters in quant path?
noah: yes, but we need regression tests. add unit that asserts monotonic kv.index for runs up to 100k tokens and fail if wrap occurs.
cheng: also add a fuzz test that places anchors at positions: [65534, 65535, 65536, 65537] with random token spikes and run both quant and float.
sam: I'll file an issue and request a small PR.
isabel: filed: https://git.internal/rwd/serving/issues/3421 — includes repro script + sample fixtures.
ci-bot: regression test job queued: longctx-fuzz-3421 on qtest-ml-14
ops-bot: rolling canary disabled on qtest-ml-12 until fix merged.
noah: great triage. lucy/sam, can you own the PR? aim to land in next patch window.
lucy-ml: on it. will prototype uint32 change + add unit + re-run repro matrix (quant4, int4, float32) and report.
cheng: when you have green results, let's run A/B on a handful of production traces (anonymized) to ensure no perf regress.
isabel: thanks all — keeping this thread for results. :thumbsup:
